data.content_ref: inline:All five neighborhood candidates depend on a single covering principle: the answer to 'how many pieces' is determined by two interpretive choices — (1) whether cuts are idealized as zero-width lines or physical kerfs, and (2) whether 'pieces' are counted combinatorially (as regions bounded by cut lines) or topologically (as connected components of the remainder). Each candidate is a projection of one combination: SRC_003 (zero-width + topological = 1 piece), SRC_004 (positive-width or fractal + topological = infinite), SRC_002 (general-position + combinatorial = 11), SRC_005 (kerf + topological = count depends on center singularity), SRC_001 (zero-width + topological = 1). The principle is REFUTED IF any candidate cannot be mapped to a unique coordinate in this two-axis space, or if a candidate's mechanism requires an interpretive dimension beyond cut-width and piece-definition.
